transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. I guess I came in because my worry’s gotten… harder to manage. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it feels like I can’t really shut my brain off anymore.

It can start with something pretty normal, like a client not responding to an email, and then within a few minutes I’m already thinking I’m going to lose the contract, fall behind on divorce payments, and never get back into a real leadership role. I know that probably sounds like a lot of jumping ahead, but it’s been happening more and more, and I’m not doing a great job stopping it on my own.
Do you find that your anxiety tends to pop up across different areas of your life—like work, relationships, and personal responsibilities—or is it usually focused on one specific thing?

It’s… not just one thing, no. I wish it were, honestly, because then maybe I could contain it better.

It jumps around a lot. One minute I’m worried about contract work, then it’s mortgage payments, then I’m thinking about whether people in the Bethesda tech circles see me as, I don’t know, damaged goods or not someone they’d want to bring in. Even something like a recruiter taking too long to answer an email can start to feel like proof that my whole career is closing down.

I know that may sound like I’m overconnecting things, but that’s how it feels in the moment.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, trouble sleeping, or muscle tension, that seem to go along with this worry?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but I do feel pretty wound up a lot of the day.

It’s like my shoulders are kind of locked all the time, and I’m bracing for bad news even when nothing is actually happening. I’ll catch myself pacing around the house, or bouncing my leg during calls, and then I feel a little embarrassed because there isn’t always a clear reason for it.

Does that… fit with what you’re asking?
Have you noticed yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends?

I’m not sure I’d say “down” exactly. I mean, I have off days, like anyone would, but I haven’t really thought of it as losing interest in things.

I still try to keep up with people and normal stuff when I can. Sometimes I’m just distracted or preoccupied, I guess. But I don’t want to over-label it if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find that your worrying feels uncontrollable or that you can't stop it, even when you try?

Yeah… unfortunately, yes. I’ve tried to talk myself out of it, like, “Okay, this is just one client not replying, don’t make it bigger than it is,” but it doesn’t really stop there.

It’s like my brain grabs onto it and starts building the whole worst-case chain. A client doesn’t respond, and within minutes I’m thinking I’m going to lose the contract, then I’ll fall behind on divorce payments, and then I’m never going to get back into a real leadership role again.

I know that sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, and I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, but… that’s honestly part of why I came in. I can’t seem to shut my brain off anymore. Is that the kind of uncontrollable worry you mean?
How long have you been experiencing this kind of constant worry and physical tension?

I guess… it’s been about thirteen months now. It really started after I was fired, and I kept thinking it would settle down once I found some contract work.

And it helped a little in practical terms, obviously, but the worry and the tension never really went away. It’s kind of embarrassing to admit it’s been that long, but… that’s probably the honest answer.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious even when there’s no specific trigger, like when you’re just sitting quietly or doing something routine?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s not always tied to one clear thing.

Even if I’m just sitting there or doing something normal, I’ll notice I’m kind of wound up, like my shoulders are locked and I’m bracing for bad news. I’ll pace around the house or bounce my leg during calls, even when nothing is actually happening.

I don’t know if that counts as anxious exactly, but it feels like I’m ready for something to go wrong most of the day.
